speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment what measures will be introduced to ensure that supermarkets and other corporate entities do not pass on the costs of adopting sustainability-friendly measures to consumers.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Consumers are increasingly demanding sustainable products and services.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Consumers are also choosing to buy from businesses with more sustainable practices.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Businesses have responded by adopting more sustainable practices and introducing greener goods and services.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The pricing of these products and services is part of this commercial decision.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In some cases, products and services may cost a bit more.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But in a competitive market, businesses will compete to provide consumers with the most value-for-money products and services.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As sustainable products and services become more mainstream, economies of scale could bring down costs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There could also be cost savings from going green.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, energy-efficient products may cost more upfront but provide savings over their life cycle.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Packaging serves an important function of reducing damage, minimising cross-contamination and enhancing the shelf-life of certain food types, thereby reducing wastage of food products.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Supermarkets and businesses can preserve the quality of their products through more sustainable packaging models, such as reusable and refillable packaging.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I encourage businesses to minimise waste in their use of packaging and consumers to avoid the excessive use of packaging.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I am very happy that we have this Packaging Partnership Programme.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I realise it has been there for a few years.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Would the Minister know how has the take-up rate for this programme improved over the years or has it stayed the same?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: And how are the companies being encouraged to take up this Packaging Partnership Programme so that consumers would have a wider range of choices who prefer food products or packages that have greener carbon footprints because I realise that they can actually put a logo for reduced packaging for these particular companies?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As I have mentioned, this Packaging Partnership Programme is something new that we have launched in 2021.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They are across the entire packaging supply chain from packaging, manufacturing and logistics service providers to retailers, such as supermarkets.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is for sustainable packaging, and we hope that more companies will come on board and we hope that the programme, through its time, will bring about more sustainable packaging practices into the market.

speaker: Mr Speaker

speaker: Mr Speaker
